verdict.rationale: The skills CLI documents a non-interactive, explicitly 'CI/CD friendly' install mode (`-y` with `--skill`/`-a`/`-g`), lockfile restore via `skills install`, and `skills use` piping a prompt to stdout. A hands-on probe confirmed it runs keylessly from npm and switches itself to promptless mode when driven by an agent. Missing for 10: a documented CI pipeline example (e.g. a GitHub Actions recipe) and documented exit-code/error-handling behavior for automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote:
# Non-interactive installation (CI/CD friendly)
npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill frontend-design -g -a claude-code -y

the skills CLI ran keylessly from npm — `npx -y skills --version` printed 1.5.24 with no account, and it auto-detected it was being driven by a coding agent ('claude-code_2-1-245_agent — installing non-interactively'), switching to promptless mode by itself.
`skills use` resolves sources the same way as `skills add`, writes the selected skill files to a temporary directory, and prints only the generated prompt to stdout unless `--agent` is provided.
